'''''Mandevilla laxa''''', commonly known as '''Chilean jasmine''',<ref name="Botanica 562">"Botanica. The Illustrated AZ of over 10000 garden plants and how to cultivate them", pp. 562-563. Könemann, 2004. {{ISBN|3-8331-1253-0}}</ref><ref name="GRIN">{{GRIN | accessdate=2012-12-15}}</ref> is an [[ornamental plant]] in the genus ''[[Mandevilla]]'' of family [[Apocynaceae]].

''M. laxa'' is native to southern [[Ecuador]], [[Peru]], [[Bolivia]], and northern [[Argentina]].<ref name="GRIN"/> It grows as a [[vine]] and is [[deciduous]] in cool climates. It can grow to 6 meters (20 feet) tall. Masses of heavily scented white flowers are produced in the summer.<ref name="Botanica 562"/> As it is not fully [[hardiness (plants)|hardy]] and does not survive being frozen, in [[temperate climate|temperate]] zones it must be grown with the protection of glass, in an unheated greenhouse or conservatory. with full sunlight. In the [[United Kingdom]] it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/50035/i-Mandevilla-laxa-i/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Mandevilla laxa'' 
| accessdate=4 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf 
| title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 64 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 4 April 2018}}</ref>

Despite its common name 'Chilean jasmine', the species is not a [[Jasmine#Other plants called "jasmine"|true jasmine]] of the genus ''[[Jasminum]]''.
